tile.compliance_2025: In the first year of its new policy, nearly four in five Gates-funded publications complied, most without the foundation paying a publishing fee.
tile.preprints_lmic_2025: Almost two in three Gates-funded preprints in 2025 had an author based in a low- or middle-income country, up from just over half in 2024 and in line with the foundation’s focus on global health research funding.
tile.head_start_median_2025: By promoting preprints, the foundation helps findings reach others sooner: in 2025, preprinted research was public a median of 7.6 months before its journal article.

comparison.preprints_and_cc_by_share: In the policy’s second year, grantees are posting more preprints, and more of them meet the policy: 78% so far in 2026, up from 65% at this point in 2025.
comparison.das: More grantees are being transparent about the data behind their research: 78% of articles from early 2026 included a data availability statement, up slightly on 2025.
comparison.preprint_growth: Preprints rose by 80% in the first year of the new policy, as grantees increasingly turn to preprints to share their findings sooner.
comparison.lmic_authors: Since the new policy began, 12% more Gates-funded publications have included authors in low- and middle-income countries, now two in three of the total. That’s in line with the foundation’s focus on global health research funding.
